correctness.rationale: The claimed lower rational degree is 2k for n=6k>=12, whereas the cited Agarwal–Basak nonequivariant base B_n has homology only at 3k-1>2k; hence the long exact relative sequence gives a natural G-equivariant identification H_{2k}(X_n)=H_{2k}(X_n,B_n). The exact matching-extension decomposition X_n=B_n∪P_0∪P_1 with two exceptional alternating rim simplices and each B_n∩P_i=Ind(C_n) identifies the relative module as induction from the index-two stabilizer H=<rs,ts> of W=H_{2k-1}(Ind(C_n);Q). For n=6k the cycle independence polynomial at -1 gives rotation traces 2cos(pi a/3) and both reflection-axis traces zero in odd degree; induction and central layer swap split as rho_{n/6}⊠1 plus rho_{n/3}⊠epsilon, giving the displayed casewise G-character and vanishing invariants. Independent signed invariant-orbit enumeration on cycle lengths 6,12,18 reproduced all 72 rotation/reflection traces, and the package test source checks width-12 relative action. The exact all-width matching-extension and B_n homotopy lemmas are nonstandard published inputs; their full v2 article was not accessible this run (Oxford VPN disconnected), so citation-to-input reliance is explicitly retained, not falsely called independently re-proved. No inference from finite checks to all n.
